title: Block Any Home Wi-Fi Device From Anywhere, One Tap | vitalii.no
description:
Family Link doesn't see the PlayStation, the TV stick, or a guest laptop — now one tap blocks any of them, from anywhere.

Google Family Link only covers devices it's installed on. The Android TV stick, the PlayStation, and random guest laptops stayed invisible to it, and the router's own admin page only worked from inside the house. There was no single place to see every device on the home Wi-Fi, let alone block one the moment it mattered, from wherever a parent actually was.

A Cloudflare Worker now serves both the API and a static PWA, backed by a D1 database. A home agent written in Python talks directly to the router's web UI, including a from-scratch port of its own SRP-6a login flow, reads the live device table and Wi-Fi usage, and applies blocks through the router's own access-control rules. The agent runs in the background on Windows, Linux, or a spare Android phone, polling the Worker over HTTPS.

Every device on the home Wi-Fi now shows up automatically with an editable name and today's real usage, and a one-tap block works identically from home Wi-Fi, from 5G, or from someone else's network — enforced on the router itself, not on a device that could just be swapped out.
